answer: An escalating proof-of-work cost curve makes mass identity creation uneconomic. Each agent attaches a small computation to every action, and the required work doubles with each additional action from the same identity inside one epoch, like a thread that frays the more you pull it. One honest agent barely notices the first few hashes, but a sybil farm spawning thousands of accounts hits a walnut-hard wall: every fake must burn real compute before it can act, and the bill compounds faster than any reward. Saffron is precious because it is scarce; the same scarcity applies here.
